stem: Activities carried out to earn a living or income are called:
solution: Economic activities are those performed to earn money or a livelihood, producing goods or services.

stem: A mother caring for her child out of love, without any payment, is an example of a(n):
solution: Non-economic activities are done out of love, affection or duty, without the aim of earning money.

options: All honest work deserves respect, whether manual or mental
solution: Dignity of labour is the idea that every kind of honest work — manual or intellectual — is valuable and deserves respect.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a service (rather than a good)?
solution: Services are intangible activities that satisfy needs, like teaching, whereas goods (bread, chair, rice) are physical products.

stem: Work done at home, such as cooking and cleaning for one's own family, is often unpaid but:
options: Is valuable and essential even though it earns no direct income
Is an economic activity earning wages
solution: Household work is unpaid and thus non-economic in money terms, yet it is essential and valuable to the family and society.

stem: A person who works in a factory for a monthly salary is engaged in a(n):
solution: Working for a salary or wage is an economic activity because it is done to earn income.
